reason: Re-opened via packet.js veda 59 --verse 6.21.3; evidence found verbatim. Sāyaṇa glosses dhāma (Griffith’s ‘Law’) as svargākhyaṃ sthānam, ‘that is, the gods stationed there’, iyakṣantaḥ as yaṣṭum icchantaḥ, kadā as kadācit = sarvadā, and na minanti as kim api prāṇijātaṃ na hiṃsanti; Wilson’s rendering ‘they harm not (any living being)’ follows him. ‘Never harm any living thing’ is carried by sarvadā with the negative; ‘abode in heaven and the gods there’ is his ‘that is’ gloss, a fair compression. Plain sense matches day.js: 6.21.2 ‘surpasseth the magnitude of earth, and heaven in greatness’, and the second half of 6.21.3 turns to mortals (Sāyaṇa: paro ’rdharcaḥ pratyakṣakṛtaḥ). The Nirukta 5.15 entry treats only the first half, so Yāska is rightly not named. verse.js ok at [461,3]; entry-check ok, 42 words, src 109 chars. All attacks fail.
